title: Odd Elasticity in Strain-Gradient Continua: Anisotropy Classification and Non-Hermitian Elastodynamics
abstract: Odd elasticity extends continuum mechanics to active nonconservative systems containing internal energy sources, such as robotic active metamaterials with nonreciprocal feedback. Modeling these systems as effective continua requires relaxing Maxwell-Betti reciprocity, which results in stiffness tensors lacking major symmetry. In this contribution, we extend this framework to 3D strain-gradient odd elasticity to incorporate the length scales inherent in these heterogeneous systems. By applying the full hierarchy of 3D point-group symmetries along chiral and achiral branches, we derive the exhaustive set of fourth-, fifth-, and sixth-order odd elastic stiffness tensors. Further, utilizing the dynamic principle of virtual work, we formulate the equilibrium equations, higher-order boundary conditions, and the generalized acoustic tensor for elastodynamic analysis. The results demonstrate that nonreciprocal moduli survive even under full isotropy in the sixth-order stiffness, under hemitropy in the fifth-order stiffness, and under cubic symmetry in fourth-order stiffness. In contrast, the elastodynamic analysis reveals that under isotropic and hemitropic limits, despite the underlying odd stiffness moduli, the acoustic tensor remains unconditionally Hermitian. Non-Hermitian elastodynamics is shown to require anisotropy. By numerically analyzing a transversely hemitropic odd elastic continuum, we demonstrate that this symmetry reduction results in non-Hermitian elastodynamic phenomena including exceptional points in the dispersion spectra and active energy exchange through simultaneous amplification and attenuation of the elastic wave components. These results provide the necessary theoretical foundation for future multiscale homogenization frameworks for anisotropic strain-gradient active microstructures, and for the design of nonreciprocal strain-gradient metamaterials.
summary: This work develops a comprehensive theoretical framework for odd elasticity in 3D strain-gradient continua to model active metamaterials. By analyzing symmetry constraints, the authors show that non-Hermitian wave dynamics, including exceptional points, only emerge when the material possesses sufficient anisotropy. This provides a foundation for designing non-reciprocal, active microstructures.
main_problem: The paper extends continuum mechanics to model active, nonconservative systems by incorporating strain-gradient effects, which necessitates relaxing Maxwell-Betti reciprocity.
main_result: Non-Hermitian elastodynamics, characterized by exceptional points and active energy exchange, is shown to require material anisotropy, even when higher-order stiffness tensors are derived.
method: The authors systematically derive exhaustive sets of fourth-, fifth-, and sixth-order odd elastic stiffness tensors by applying 3D point-group symmetries and formulating equilibrium equations via the virtual work principle.
model_or_system: The model is 3D strain-gradient odd elasticity, designed for active metamaterials and nonconservative systems that violate standard energy potential assumptions.
key_observables: Odd elastic stiffness tensors, the generalized acoustic tensor (diagnosed for Hermitian/non-Hermitian behavior), and exceptional points in the dispersion spectra.
important_parameters: Strain-gradient length scales ($\ell$), symmetry types (isotropic, hemitropic, cubic), and the perturbation parameter ($\varepsilon$).
main_assumptions: The primary assumption is that the system is active and nonconservative, leading to the breakdown of Maxwell-Betti reciprocity.
figures_summary: The notes refer to a hierarchy of elastic symmetry classes (Figure 1) and detailed component counts for different point groups (Table B.2).
paper_structure: The paper progresses from establishing the need for odd elasticity, to deriving the symmetry constraints for higher-order stiffness tensors, and finally performing numerical elastodynamic analysis on a specific anisotropic case.
why_interesting: While focused on solid mechanics, the emergence of non-Hermitian dynamics, exceptional points, and active energy exchange provides a direct theoretical framework applicable to open quantum systems and non-reciprocal quantum devices.

figures.caption: Figure 1: Hierarchy of elastic symmetry classes. The upper and lower branches contain chiral and achiral symmetry groups, respectively. Solid and dashed arrows denote rotations and reflections, respectively.

Figure 2: Normalized dispersion curves for a plane wave propagating in an isotropic odd elastic continuum (solid lines with solid markers). The linear acoustic asymptotes (lines) and classical conservative strain- gradient limits (dashed lines with hollow markers) are provided for reference.

Figure 3: Normalized dispersion curves for a plane wave propagating in an odd elastic hemitropic continuum (solid lines with solid markers). The linear acoustic asymptotes (lines) and classical conservative strain- gradient limits (dashed lines with hollow markers) are provided for reference. We note the asymmetry of the transverse modes, caused by acoustical activity in chiral media, where a right-handed wave propagating forward is equivalent to a left-handed wave propagating backward (ωRCP (k) = ωLCP (−k)).

Figure 4: Dispersion analysis for an obliquely propagating wave in a transversely hemitropic odd elastic continuum: (a) the real part (solid lines with solid markers): first gradient asymptotes (lines) and classical conservative strain-gradient limits (dashed lines with hollow markers) are provided for reference, (b) the imaginary part: confirming the non-Hermitian nature of the acoustic tensor, (c) the scaled discriminant of the characteristic polynomial: showing the region with non-Hermitian behavior. (d) the coalescence of the eigenvectors of the two quasi-shear waves: showing exceptional points where eigenvectors (and eigenvalues) collide.
